blocks.heading: Diferencia entre WHO y WHOM: es que hay una preposición
formulas: PREPOSICIÓN + WHOM  (on whom · with whom · to whom)

wrong.bad: Peter, with who I spoke yesterday, ...
wrong.good: Peter, with whom I spoke yesterday, ... (después de preposición: whom)

blocks.heading: DEFINING relative clauses
blocks.rule: Add essential information · No commas · Omission of the relative pronoun as the O.D. · that = who / which.
examples: The film **(that / which)** I saw yesterday was great.

blocks.heading: NON-DEFINING relative clauses
examples: Avatar, **which is my favourite film**, was great.

wrong.bad: Avatar, that is my favourite film, was great.
wrong.good: Avatar, which is my favourite film, was great.

sections.title: B) PARTICIPLE CLAUSES
sections.subtitle: Formal grammar (to focus on a point of information)

blocks.heading: Instead of a relative clause
blocks.rule: Para usar una participle clause eliminamos el relative pronoun y el verbo.

compare.label: Relative clause
compare.text: The man **who is working** as a teacher is Álvaro.

compare.label: Participle clause
compare.text: The man **working** as a teacher is Álvaro.

blocks.heading: Speaking (Part 2)
examples: In the 1st photograph **a girl can be seen working** as ..., while the 2nd photo **shows a boy who is working** ...

compare.label: Because / so → MV-ing
compare.text: I studied a lot because I wanted to pass the test. → **Wanting** to pass the test, I studied a lot.

compare.label: As / while → MV-ing
compare.text: While I was driving home, I saw an accident. → **Driving** home, I saw an accident.

compare.label: As / while → MV-ing
compare.text: As I was studying at home, I felt sick. → **Studying** at home, I felt sick.

compare.label: And → MV-ing
compare.text: I opened the door and saw Álvaro explaining. → I opened the door, **seeing** Álvaro explaining.

compare.label: When / once / after → Having + MV-ed2
compare.text: When I had applied for the job, I ... → **Having applied** for the job, I ...

compare.label: If → MV-ed2
compare.text: If it is cooked at a low temperature, it would taste better. → **Cooked** at a low temperature, it would taste better.

blocks.heading: IF → MV-ed2: dos condiciones
blocks.rule: 1ª parte en PASIVA (it is cooked / it is used...) · el SUJETO es el mismo que el de la segunda parte.

wrong.bad: Studied this in detail, you will find it interesting. (you no eres 'estudiado')
wrong.good: Cooked at a low temperature, it would taste better. (it = la comida, que es cocinada)

blocks.heading: After the object of some verbs: see / hear / watch / notice / find
examples: I **found Peter cheating** in the exam.
I **saw my brother talking** on the phone.

sections.title: C) APPOSITION
sections.subtitle: Quitamos el relative pronoun y el verbo de una non-defining

compare.label: Relative clause
compare.text: My friends, **who are called** Peter and Mike, live in London.

compare.label: Apposition
compare.text: My friends, **Peter and Mike**, live in London.

speaking.structure: In the 1st photograph a [person] can be seen [V-ing]..., while the 2nd photo shows a [person] who is [V-ing]...
speaking.example: In the 1st photograph a girl can be seen working as a waitress, while the 2nd photo shows a boy who is studying.
speaking.translation: En la 1ª foto se ve a [persona] [haciendo algo], mientras que la 2ª muestra a [persona] que está [haciendo algo].

speaking.structure: Wanting to [goal], people nowadays tend to [action].
speaking.example: Wanting to save money, people nowadays tend to buy second-hand clothes.
speaking.translation: Queriendo [objetivo], la gente hoy en día tiende a [acción].

speaking.structure: Having [past participle], [people] find it much easier to [action].
speaking.example: Having graduated from university, young people find it much easier to get a good job.
speaking.translation: Tras haber [participio], a [la gente] le resulta mucho más fácil [acción].
